soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1: cost-optimal certificate feasibility
soundness_flags.one_line: The claimed running time contains N_E even though the input is only the physical instance and E is an existential certificate/output; state an explicit input/output-sensitive bound, e.g. in N_{E*}, and prove a size bound before using it.

soundness_flags.label: Proposition 5: positive physical separation
soundness_flags.one_line: The proposition gives numerical values and costs but supplies neither structural equations for M1,M2 nor a concrete action catalogue/cost map defining the alleged cost-one CTF-RAND and cost-two direct protocols.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 2: ordinary-subclass equivalence
soundness_flags.one_line: Dord imports Q with the general Layer-2.5 counterfactual-joint type while the Akbari ordinary-design comparator is an ordinary causal-effect problem; explicitly restrict the embedded Q to the ordinary query subclass and give its translation.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: CTFIDU+ takes a graph, an unnested query, and a supplied set of input distributions; it searches those inputs factorwise and is sound and complete for identification from that fixed input collection.
The paper defines counterfactual realizability and gives a complete procedure for determining whether a counterfactual distribution can be sampled under physical constraints.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3-4, Theorem 1; p. 4, Lemma 3; p. 4, Theorem 2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: For a single c-component target, a no-more-costly singleton collection exists; the optimum is a weighted hitting set over hedges; weighted minimum vertex cover reduces to the minimum-cost intervention problem.
The paper reformulates ordinary minimum-cost proxy experiment design using weighted Max-SAT and integer programming, after identifying the earlier ordinary MCID problem as NP-complete.
The paper extends structural causal bandits to realizable counterfactual actions and relies on counterfactual randomization/realizability for accessible Layer-3 data.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make the computational contract explicit: define the input encoding, prove a canonical certificate-size bound, and replace the free N_E term by a bound in |I|, parameters, and the encoded output length.
Add a fully tabulated binary separation witness: structural equations for both SCMs, all 27 ordinary-regime laws, exact CTF-RAND slice calculation, and the two protocol catalogues with costs.
Restrict Dord and the two-way embedding to a named ordinary-query subclass, then prove that its Layer-2.5 encoding and source-family semantics exactly match Akbari et al.'s Q[S] formulation.

Elevate the field kernel only after the normal-form question is resolved: state a generic-class theorem showing when assignment-uniform source selection succeeds or a concrete counterexample characterizing the required extra certificate object.

recommended_next_step: Revise the three semantic interfaces—complexity input/output size, explicit separation construction, and ordinary-query embedding—then retain the field-level novelty angle for Stage 0.
